title: Review Japan Mod
text:
Mo, I found **Japan Rising R13.1** on the [`japan-rising` branch of your repository](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/tree/japan-rising), and reviewed revision **`1a04a729`**.

**My verdict: this has the foundations of an enjoyable, ambitious Japanese campaign, particularly through the main wars. I would fix two campaign-threatening logic issues before committing 10–15 days to a main save. The other substantial weakness is the limited depth after victory.**

I reviewed the original specification, the final event catalogue, the code that transforms it, economic and unit changes, AI changes, and existing tests. This is a source and campaign-design review; I have not played this release in Darkest Hour.

## 1. What you have built—and why

The central design is coherent: **give Japan enough resilience to pursue a long campaign, while preserving the familiar historical opening through Pearl Harbor.** Subsequent wars are largely independent, so the player can combine Pacific, Indian Ocean, Soviet and American ambitions.

The changes address specific problems documented in your earlier campaigns:

| Area | What the expansion does | Problem it addresses |
|---|---|---|
| Industry and resources | Adds funded industrial development, domestic fuel/mineral works, storage and paid fuel conversion | More factories and larger forces were becoming unsustainable because of resource shortages |
| Army, air force and navy | Offers separate production priorities, repair support and recruitment reserves | Replacing losses and maintaining a broad military were becoming impractical |
| China | Adds decisive and limited settlements, proper national territory, reconstruction and partner roles | Conquest did not reliably produce a useful Chinese settlement or ally |
| India and other countries | Adds named settlement choices, bases, access, starter support and selected regional programmes | Capturing territory needed a useful political and military aftermath |
| Strategic endings | Adds a Pacific armistice, American national-defeat terms and a separate Soviet settlement | Winning needed achievable endpoints beyond occupying everything |
| Japanese identity | Adds specialist equipment, research institutions, personnel work and distinct artwork | Japan needed interesting capabilities and development choices |
| Opponents and partners | Repairs parts of Allied transport protection and Axis endurance | Weak AI behaviour could undermine the wider campaign |

That understanding comes from the [original campaign specification](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/JAPAN_EXPANSION_SPEC.md) and the [current campaign overview](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/README.md).

**I would preserve this direction.** A historical opening followed by several plausible military outcomes suits this campaign well.

## 2. How I think it will feel to play

These are my design judgments, rather than observed playtest results.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Fun and ambition** | Strong potential. There are useful things to prepare, capture, develop and negotiate. |
| **Player agency** | Good operational freedom. Production choices generally leave unrelated wars available. |
| **Event content** | Substantial, with considerable support machinery beneath it. Narrative depth varies between countries. |
| **Meaningful decisions** | Several good trade-offs; some major diplomatic choices need stronger consequences. |
| **Balance** | Japan should be more sustainable. Whether Hard remains challenging is unproven. |
| **Alternate timelines** | Multiple military outcomes are implemented in source. Some combinations have incomplete handling. |
| **Long-campaign payoff** | Stronger during expansion and war; considerably thinner after the main victories. |
| **Reliability** | Extensive defensive scripting exists, but I found important gaps in the final catalogue. |

For perspective, the custom catalogue contains **1,822 event definitions and 121 registered decision cards**. **Twenty-six cards are deliberately disabled**, leaving **95 potentially available custom cards**, subject to their conditions. A large portion of the event count consists of support, delivery and settlement handlers. These counts exclude the inherited Blood and Iron experience. [Final catalogue](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/events.json)

The most promising stretch is **China through the wider Pacific war**: preparing a force, earning a settlement, establishing partners, securing resources, then choosing another ambition. My concern is what keeps the campaign compelling after those systems have paid off.

## 3. Two issues I would fix before your main campaign

### A. China can replace an army you spent years helping it build

**This is the most serious finding.**

The Chinese reorganisation event, `cn_reorganise` / **28601657**, checks China’s **current** army size. It does not record whether that army was inherited at settlement or built subsequently.

A possible sequence is:

1. You settle China with fewer than 96 qualifying formations.
2. The reorganisation does not activate.
3. China develops for several years and grows beyond that threshold.
4. China reaches peace.
5. The old event becomes eligible, removes Chinese land forces and replaces them with **96 preset formations**.
6. Only **32 can move immediately**; the remaining groups unlock after one and two years.

The source has no settlement-age limit or completed assessment for a smaller inherited army. Its removal commands cover the named continents before activating the replacement formations. [Reorganisation code and templates](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/campaign_balance.py#L41-L78)

The engine’s documented removal command also reaches units redeploying or embarked in the specified area, so its potential scope is substantial. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

I reproduced the eligibility problem in a narrow check of the published event conditions. The existing tests cover a large army being reorganised and a small army failing the condition immediately; they do not cover **that small army growing later**.

**Recommended fix:** assess the inherited army during settlement and close that assessment even when no reorganisation is needed. Any integration restrictions should target the inherited formations, preserving subsequent production.

For a long campaign, protecting earned progress takes priority.

### B. Changing alliances during peace implementation can strand negotiations

Formal Axis entry remains available while American or Soviet negotiations are pending. However, later implementation events require Japan to remain outside Germany’s alliance.

If you join between accepting terms and their implementation:

- The implementation event can have **no valid action**.
- The pending negotiation state is not cleared.
- Leaving the Axis later may still leave the original peace decision unavailable.

This exists in the final American `us_implement` and Soviet `soviet_land` events. I reproduced the conflicting conditions in a source-level fixture; the precise in-game presentation remains untested. [Peace sequences and Axis entry](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/endings.py#L19-L46)

**Recommended fix:** add explicit recovery when alliance or war conditions change. The process should cancel cleanly or resume from its actual state, including any territorial transfers already completed.

## 4. Decisions and alternate timelines need a few stronger connections

### Coalition victories are not consistently recognised

Several settlements require **Japan itself** to control their key objectives. India, for example, requires Japanese control of Delhi and either Calcutta or Bombay. Soviet terms similarly require direct Japanese control of the listed objectives.

A partner controlling one of those cities can therefore prevent the expected settlement from appearing. The Pacific armistice already accepts allied control of Singapore and Manila, showing that the broader treatment exists elsewhere. [Country conditions](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/catalog.py#L251-L273) · [Pacific and Soviet conditions](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/endings.py#L8-L38)

Darkest Hour explicitly distinguishes a named country’s control from allied control. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

**Player impact:** building useful partners can make a coalition victory less compatible with the settlement scripts.

The fix needs an agreed coalition settlement and ownership checks. Simply allowing Japan to dispose of every ally’s conquest would create another problem.

### Returning Hawaii buys no explicit diplomatic concession

America accepts negotiations **before** Japan chooses whether to return or retain Hawaii. Both options then lead to the same peace and non-aggression arrangement.

Returning Hawaii does not improve acceptance, accelerate peace, preserve trade or obtain another concession. The return option’s flag has no subsequent use in the final catalogue. [American terms](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/endings.py#L19-L30)

There is still a territorial and defence commitment involved in holding Hawaii. But as a negotiation, the choice is underdeveloped.

**I would put the demands before the American response:** returning Hawaii could secure earlier peace or commercial normalisation; keeping it could require stronger military leverage and produce a more hostile aftermath.

There is a related peace-balance concern: one qualifying condition accepts **four cumulative American carrier losses**, irrespective of how many carriers America has subsequently rebuilt. The territorial hold remains demanding, but that branch does not establish continuing naval superiority. [Armistice eligibility](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/endings.py#L8-L16)

## 5. The final years need more substance

This is the largest content gap relative to your intended 1933–1950 experience.

Several proposed late programmes—next-generation fleet and aircraft development, the 1948 reserve and 1949 research programme—are explicitly disabled in the current catalogue. [Retirement list](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/human_campaign.py#L9-L18)

After 1943, I found only **four newly dated active strategic decision cards**:

| Year | New strategic decision |
|---|---|
| 1945 | Civilian reconstruction |
| 1947 | Chinese autonomy |
| 1947 | Indian autonomy |
| 1947 | Civilian shipyard conversion versus merchant reconstruction |

Earlier unfinished decisions, ongoing wars, specialist upgrades and delayed treaty events can still provide activity. Nevertheless, the developed political aftermath is much lighter than the [original specification’s late-campaign ambitions](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/JAPAN_EXPANSION_SPEC.md#L284-L301).

**For someone investing two weeks, winning should open a compelling final chapter.** I would prioritise three connected situations:

- **America after peace:** relations and rearmament respond to the severity of the settlement.
- **China and India after consolidation:** autonomy, military obligations and base agreements create recurring political choices.
- **Japan after mobilisation:** demobilisation, civilian recovery and continued military readiness compete for resources.

These should develop consequences over time. A one-off supply payment to settle a major autonomy question offers limited replay value.

## 6. Balance: preserve the improvements, verify the combined effects

### The new economy solves a real problem

The domestic works and fuel conversion have bills, lead times and operating costs. Balanced development provides more industrial minerals; fuel priority sacrifices those minerals for additional oil and coal. Both can make sense depending on your conquests and imports.

The strategic question is whether the domestic solution reduces the importance of southern oil too far.

Under the project’s stated assumptions:

- Both balanced works plus a sustained large conversion cycle provide approximately **176 oil/day**.
- Its illustrative force-activity scenario consumes approximately **165/day before combat adjustments**.
- The conversion cycle itself consumes approximately **267 energy, 18 supplies and 2.2 money/day**.

These are planning calculations, and actual combat consumption and shipping remain unmeasured. [Economic calculations and assumptions](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/ENDURANCE_AUDIT.md#L26-L55)

My tuning objective would be: **domestic investment enables recovery; secure southern resources materially increase the operational tempo you can sustain.**

### Specialist costs need a complete production comparison

Matsu escorts illustrate the risk:

| Comparison | Matsu | Ordinary destroyer | Matsu cost advantage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Base IC-days | 360.75 | 741 | 51.3% |
| Including the documented assembly reduction and escort-production programme | 181.33 | 491.17 | **63.1%** |

The second row is illustrative source arithmetic, excluding ministers, policies, gearing, doctrine and engine rounding. Matsu’s lower speed, range and surface capability remain meaningful disadvantages. [Specialist costs and trade-offs](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/R13_UNITS.md#L20-L31) · [Assembly assumptions](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/CONSTRUCTION_BALANCE.md#L42-L46)

The existing combined construction check omits the newer specialist classes `d_13`–`d_19`. Their introduction and modifier inheritance have tests, but that does not establish balanced final production costs. [Construction coverage](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/construction_review.py#L22-L34)

### Opponent challenge remains an open question

The starting transport repair is sensible: it reallocates existing screens and adjusts future construction priorities. The code acknowledges that the engine can subsequently regroup fleets. It establishes a real initial improvement, while sustained Allied invasion competence remains unverified. [Transport AI changes](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/enemy_transport_ai.py)

Two other gaps deserve targeted checks:

- **India with at least 20 IC skips the custom initial land-AI assignment**, retaining its ordinary inherited/release AI until another applicable change. That weakens the promise of a reliably useful regional partner. [Support policy](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/release_support.py#L64-L85)
- **The added American mainland reserve waves use fixed 1939/1936 infantry**, including during a late invasion. Normal American production continues, but the expansion’s emergency response has limited scaling. [American reserve response](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/us_campaign_content.py#L86-L109)

I would not certify Hard balance from the current evidence.

## 7. Are there genuinely different campaign options?

**Yes—several substantial military and diplomatic paths exist in the source.** Their readiness differs:

| Campaign direction | My assessment |
|---|---|
| Historical opening, early Chinese victory, then Pacific war | The clearest intended experience |
| Limited Chinese peace versus decisive settlement | Meaningfully different outcomes |
| Unified Chinese partner versus regional partners | Real choice, subject to fixing army reorganisation |
| Southern empire and Indian Ocean expansion | Broad support; country-specific narrative depth varies |
| Separate Soviet war after Pearl Harbor | Explicitly supported despite the historical 1933 choice |
| Limited Pacific victory | Substantial alternative to invading America; negotiation logic needs refinement |
| American invasion and national surrender | Dedicated milestones and surrender handling exist |
| Formal Axis membership | Real commitment with disclosed consequences for separate peace |
| Victorious empire through 1950 | Supported dates and equipment progression; lighter political content |

The relevant implementation spans the [Chinese partner chains](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/partners.py), [major-power endings](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/endings.py) and [American national surrender](https://github.com/mohsinfd/a-union-before-midnight/blob/1a04a7290a6183197a330eb63d995edadae0af6d/japan_expansion/us_invasion.py).

**Military replayability is currently stronger than political replayability.** Different wars and force compositions should change the experience considerably; different settlements need to change the subsequent world more visibly.

## My recommendation for the next revision

| Priority | Work | Why it matters to your campaign |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Fix the delayed Chinese army replacement | Protects years of earned progress |
| **2** | Repair interrupted peace sequences and coalition settlement handling | Makes different war combinations dependable |
| **3** | Strengthen American bargaining and post-peace consequences | Gives pivotal choices lasting value |
| **4** | Check every active specialist with the full production modifier stack | Prevents one composition becoming the obvious answer |
| **5** | Develop the 1945–1950 aftermath | Gives victory a satisfying continuation |
| **6** | Verify actual opponent operations, partner production and fuel demand on Hard | Establishes whether the stronger Japan still faces a serious challenge |

For this review, the repository’s source check passed; I also matched all **209 manifest-listed files** against their canonical Git contents, verified the final catalogue hash, and found no missing custom targets among **2,748 event/trigger command references**. The two high-priority condition problems above were independently reproduced against that final catalogue. Startup, save/reload, combat, actual fleet behaviour and long-campaign stability remain unverified here.

**I would keep the economic resilience, independent war choices and specialist identity. The next revision should concentrate on protecting campaign progress and making victories produce richer consequences. Those improvements would do the most to justify your 10–15-day investment.**
